title: WIN-014: gravitational sensitivity-floor defense neutralization
defense_summary: The dome's defense: the null at C1-C4 does not refute WIN-014 because the gravimeters (especially the 7 LaCoste-Romberg springs) may not be sensitive enough to detect the predicted κ-gravity signal — absence of detection, not absence of effect. Curmudgeon c12 rated it defense_survives=3 with three prongs: (1) the precision citation covers SGs but 7/8 instruments were springs; (2) the 2013 paper's own conclusion is sensitivity-framed; (3) SG-053's location is unpinned — if off-path, the only sub-µGal instrument never saw totality.
analyst_assessment: The defense's instrument-class observation is genuine (kernel credited in patch text) but the defense is structurally self-defeating: κ's denominator (Mohe 6.5 µGal, 1997) was measured with a SINGLE LaCoste-Romberg model D spring (D-122) at the instrument's own stated 2–3 µGal precision and ±3–4 µGal residual band — verified this run directly from the primary source (arXiv:1003.4947 = Phys. Rev. D 62, 041101(R)). Any sensitivity standard strict enough to excuse the 2009 eight-instrument network from bounding a 3–9 µGal prediction annihilates the single-spring 6.5 µGal 1997 claim first, deleting κ and PRED-TIER-3's 10–13 µGal target. Authorship continuity verified from primary sources: Wang Qian-Shen AND Hua Chang-Cai appear on BOTH the 1997/2000 anomaly paper and the 2013 null paper — the discovering group itself withdrew the signal (2002 reanalysis: no significant anomaly; 2003 Van Flandern & Yang: no unambiguous detections in 30 years; 2013: weather attribution). Analyst re-rating: defense_survives=1 after patches (the defense can still be uttered, but the patched text makes it cost the defender κ).

A final defender retreat deserves formal closure because it is the strongest remaining: the claim that the network — seven of whose eight instruments were LaCoste-Romberg spring gravimeters — simply lacked the sensitivity to see a κ-coupled pulse, so the null is an absence of detection rather than evidence of absence. The instrument-class observation is correct, and it is the same observation our review makes against the 1997 Mohe measurement (WIN-011). But the defense proves far too much: κ's denominator — the 6.5 µGal Mohe anomaly — was itself measured with a single LaCoste-Romberg model D spring gravimeter (instrument D-122) whose own authors state a precision of 2–3 µGal and a residual noise band of ±3–4 µGal, against claimed contact-phase dips of 6.0 ± 2.5 and 7.0 ± 2.7 µGal (Wang et al. 2000, Phys. Rev. D 62, 041101(R)) — a 2.4–2.6σ excursion on an instrument operating at its own stated floor. If LaCoste-Romberg springs at ~1–2 µGal post-fit floors cannot bound a predicted 3–9 µGal signal in 2009 — eight instruments whose records can be epoch-folded at each site's known contact times, so that a real κ-coupled pulse would appear coherently across the network while stacking suppresses uncorrelated noise by √8 ≈ 2.8×, putting the effective network floor near 0.4–0.7 µGal, some 4–25× below the prediction — then a single spring of the same class in 1997, with no coherence check possible, certainly cannot establish the 6.5 µGal anomaly that is κ's denominator. The sensitivity defense does not rescue WIN-014; it deletes κ — and with it PRED-TIER-3's 10–13 µGal August 2026 target. The dome's own cited literature completes the circle: the 2013 record's author list includes Wang Qian-Shen and Hua Chang-Cai, both authors of the original 1997 Mohe paper, and its abstract attributes that earlier anomaly to ‘the drastic changes in the weather’ — after the same lead author's 2002 reanalysis had already reported no significant eclipse anomaly under added controls (Yang & Wang 2002) and his co-author's 2003 follow-up concluded there had been no unambiguous detections in thirty years (Van Flandern & Yang 2003). The research group that discovered the dome's denominator ran the better experiment, found nothing, and withdrew the original signal. (One verification remains open: the 2013 record's Chinese full text presumably locates the single SG-053 superconducting gravimeter; we have not located an English-language station table. Under the arithmetic above the location is moot — every possible assignment of SG-053 leaves the on-path prediction multiples above even the spring-only floor, and a defender who discards the springs discards κ first.)

anticipated_objections: Objection: epoch-folding across non-co-located sites overclaims coherence. Response: contact times are deterministic per site (known to the second from Besselian elements); folding each record at its own local contact epochs before stacking is standard practice and the √8 figure applies to uncorrelated instrument noise, which is the quantity the defense invokes. Even WITHOUT stacking, each individual spring floor (1–2 µGal) sits below the 3–9 µGal on-path prediction.

Objection: the 1997 measurement might still be real; later authors only said 'very likely' weather. Response: the patch text claims withdrawal-by-discoverers, not proof of artifact — and the dome needs the 1997 signal to be BOTH real AND precise to define κ; a 2.4–2.6σ excursion at the instrument floor that its own authors no longer defend cannot carry a locked constant.
Objection: SG-053 might have been off-path after all. Response: addressed in patch text — moot under spring-only arithmetic; and discarding springs discards κ.
kernel_of_truth: The defense correctly identifies a real instrument-class asymmetry: seven of the eight 2009 instruments were LaCoste-Romberg springs, the campaign's own conclusion is sensitivity-framed, and our review elsewhere (WIN-011/012) treats this instrument class as thermally artifact-prone. That observation is genuine and the patch text credits it before showing it is self-defeating: every µGal of distrust aimed at the 2009 springs lands with greater force on the single 1997 spring that defines κ's denominator.
